Information security policy and topic-specific policies should be defined, approved by management, published, communicated to and acknowledged by relevant personnel and relevant interested parties, and reviewed at planned intervals and if significant changes occur.
Information relating to information security threats should be collected and analysed to produce threat intelligence.

Background verification checks on all candidates to become personnel should be carried out prior to joining the organization and on an ongoing basis taking into consideration applicable laws, regulations and ethics and proportional to the business requirements, the classification of the information to be accessed and the perceived risks.

Personnel of the organization and relevant interested parties should receive appropriate information security awareness, education and training and regular updates of the organization's information security policy, topic-specific policies and procedures, as relevant for their job function.
Security perimeters should be defined and used to protect areas that contain information and other associated assets.
Premises should be continuously monitored for unauthorized physical access.
Configurations, including security configurations, of hardware, software, services and networks should be established, documented, implemented, monitored and reviewed.
Information stored in information systems, devices or in any other storage media should be deleted when no longer required.

Data masking should be used in accordance with the organization's topic-specific policy on access control and other related topic-specific policies, and business requirements, taking applicable legislation into consideration.
Data leakage prevention measures should be applied to systems, networks and any other devices that process, store or transmit sensitive information.
Networks, systems and applications should be monitored for anomalous behaviour and appropriate actions taken to evaluate potential information security incidents.
Access to external websites should be managed to reduce exposure to malicious content.

Tactic: Initial Access (TA0001) | Technique: Phishing (T1566) | Description: Adversaries may send phishing messages to gain access to victim systems. All forms of phishing are electronically delivered social engineering.
Mitigation: User Training (M1017) | Users can be trained to identify social engineering techniques and spearphishing emails.

Tactic: Credential Access (TA0006) | Technique: OS Credential Dumping (T1003) | Description: Adversaries may attempt to dump credentials to obtain account login and credential material, normally in the form of a hash or a clear text password, from the operating system and software.
Mitigation: Password Policies (M1027) | Ensure password policies are set to enforce complexity and expiration. Use multi-factor authentication where possible.
Tactic: Privilege Escalation (TA0004) | Technique: Exploitation for Privilege Escalation (T1068) | Description: Adversaries may exploit software vulnerabilities in an attempt to elevate privileges.
Mitigation: Update Software (M1051) | Update software and firmware to the latest available versions to mitigate vulnerabilities.

Tactic: Lateral Movement (TA0008) | Technique: Remote Services (T1021) | Description: Adversaries may use valid accounts to log into a service specifically designed to accept remote connections, such as telnet, SSH, and RDP.
Mitigation: Network Segmentation (M1030) | Architect sections of the network to isolate critical systems, functions, or resources. Use firewalls to restrict access to these segments.

Appointing a head of the cybersecurity function (e.g., CISO) with sufficient qualifications, independence and authority.
Developing, approving, and publishing comprehensive cybersecurity policies and procedures.
Reviewing and updating cybersecurity policies and procedures periodically (at least annually) or upon significant changes.
Establishing a comprehensive methodology for cybersecurity risk management in alignment with the organization's enterprise risk management.
Developing and maintaining an accurate and up-to-date inventory of all information assets, including hardware, software, and data.
Classifying information assets based on their criticality and sensitivity according to an approved classification policy.
Enforcing the principle of least privilege and need-to-know for granting logical access to information assets.
Reviewing access rights and privileges periodically (at least every six months) for all accounts.
Implementing Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) for remote access and for all privileged accounts.
Implementing technical protection mechanisms (e.g., Endpoint Detection and Response - EDR, Antivirus) on all endpoints and servers.
Segmenting the network based on the classification of systems and data, isolating critical systems from public or non-critical networks.
Performing periodic vulnerability assessments (at least quarterly) and addressing identified vulnerabilities according to their severity.
Conducting penetration testing periodically (at least annually) or upon major changes to critical systems.
Developing, approving, and testing a comprehensive cybersecurity incident response plan.
Implementing a secure backup solution with periodic testing of data restoration capabilities.
Establishing a process to identify, assess, and manage cybersecurity risks associated with third parties prior to engagement.
Ensuring that cybersecurity requirements are explicitly included in contracts and agreements with third parties.
Conducting periodic cybersecurity audits and assessments on third parties to ensure compliance with agreed-upon requirements.
Evaluating and selecting cloud service providers based on their ability to meet the organization's cybersecurity requirements and applicable national regulations.
Ensuring data sovereignty requirements are met when hosting data in cloud environments.
Developing, approving, and implementing a cybersecurity resilience strategy that aligns with the organization's Business Continuity Management (BCM).
Identifying critical business functions and determining the Maximum Tolerable Downtime (MTD) and Recovery Time Objective (RTO) for associated information systems.
Testing the disaster recovery plan periodically (at least annually) to ensure critical systems and business operations can be recovered within the agreed RTO.
Implementing secure software development life cycle (SSDLC) practices for all business and web applications developed internally or externally.
Deploying Web Application Firewalls (WAF) to protect critical web and business applications from common web-based attacks.
Ensuring sensitive data processed by business applications (e.g., financial data, PII) is encrypted in transit and at rest.
